page: Amazon Web Services m8i.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, with 32 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a large 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 256 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities across compute and memory tasks. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core testing, software compilation with Clang, and image processing. It also delivers top-tier performance in static web serving throughput, reaching 107.39 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show strong read-only performance, with 5137.47 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 196.85 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth is moderate at 80.7 GB/sec. The processor's support for Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 enables efficient execution of vector and matrix operations, as demonstrated by top-tier prompt processing speeds of 39.74 tokens/sec for large 70B LLM models, though text generation for the same model is average at 3.49 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i.16xlarge offers high resource density and balanced compute-to-memory allocation, making it a viable option for workloads requiring substantial CPU power and fast memory access without the overhead of specialized GPU hardware. The combination of high-speed DDR5 memory and dedicated Intel Xeon cores makes this instance well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, static web serving, Redis database operations, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 256 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The instance delivers top-tier performance in multi-core benchmarks, software compilation, and static web serving, which reaches 107.39 GB/sec. It also features advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX, aiding in tasks like prompt processing for large language models. With a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, this instance is optimized for resource-dense, multi-threaded workloads. It is highly suitable for enterprise web serving, software build pipelines, Redis databases, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
